title: Left-Quillen transport and comparison of special simplicial frames
statement: Use the model-category axioms and Reedy structures of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Let $T:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:U$ be an adjunction whose left functor preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Let $Y_c$ be cofibrant and fibrant. Let $B:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal M$ be Reedy fibrant with $B_0=Y_c$ and a Reedy trivial cofibration $i:\operatorname{const}Y_c\to B$ with $i_0=1_{Y_c}$. Let $r:TY_c\to Z$ be a trivial cofibration with $Z$ fibrant. Let $B':\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal N$ be Reedy fibrant with $B'_0=Z$ and an objectwise weak-equivalence coaugmentation $i':\operatorname{const}Z\to B'$ with $i'_0=1_Z$. Then $T(i):\operatorname{const}(TY_c)\to TB$ is a Reedy trivial cofibration. There exists a natural transformation $b:TB\to B'$ satisfying $bT(i)=i'\operatorname{const}(r)$ and $b_0=r$, and every component of $b$ is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Hovey, Model Categories, Theorem 5.2.8 (printed p.128), Proposition 5.4.7 (p.132), Lemma 5.5.1 (p.133); agent extraction of the Reedy lifting and comparison argument in the parent former step 12.

proof.text:
Put $A=\operatorname{const}Y_c$ and $f=i:A\to B$. For every degree $n$, left-adjoint preservation of small colimits [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] applied to the latching diagrams and then to the pushout span gives canonical isomorphisms
$$L_n(TA)\cong T(L_nA),\qquad L_n(TB)\cong T(L_nB),\qquad (TA)_n\amalg_{L_n(TA)}L_n(TB)\cong T(A_n\amalg_{L_nA}L_nB).$$
The relative latching map of $Tf$ is, under these isomorphisms, $T(\lambda_n(f))$, where $\lambda_n(f):A_n\amalg_{L_nA}L_nB\to B_n$ is the relative latching map in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Indeed both maps restrict to $T(f_n)$ on the first pushout summand and to the image under $T$ of the latching structure map on the second; uniqueness in the pushout universal property identifies them. The latching index categories are small subcategories of slices of the small category $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, so the cited preservation statement applies, also to the empty latching diagram at $n=0$. Finally $TA=\operatorname{const}(TY_c)$, since a functor preserves identities.

source.place: Hovey Definition 5.2.2 and Theorem 5.2.5, printed pp.124-126; Stacks 0038 (categories.tex, lemma-adjoint-exact), part (1), for both colimit comparisons.

proof.text: Since $i$ is a Reedy trivial cofibration, every $\lambda_n(i)$ is a trivial cofibration by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. The hypothesis on $T$ makes $T(\lambda_n(i))$ a trivial cofibration. The identification in step 1 and the same relative-latching criterion in $\mathcal N^{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}$ show that $T(i):\operatorname{const}(TY_c)\to TB$ is a Reedy trivial cofibration. In particular every $T(i_n)$ is a weak equivalence, because Reedy weak equivalences are objectwise. This uses preservation of trivial cofibrations, and does not require a claim that $T$ preserves arbitrary weak equivalences or that $TB$ is Reedy fibrant.

source.place: Hovey Theorem 5.2.5, printed pp.125-126, trivial-cofibration criterion and objectwise weak equivalences.

proof.text: Work in the Reedy model category $\mathcal N^{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}$ of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Let $\mathbf1$ be its terminal diagram. Form the commutative square with upper arrow $i'\circ\operatorname{const}(r):\operatorname{const}(TY_c)\to B'$, left arrow $T(i):\operatorname{const}(TY_c)\to TB$, right arrow $B'\to\mathbf1$, and lower arrow the unique map $TB\to\mathbf1$. It commutes by uniqueness of maps to a terminal object. The left arrow is a trivial cofibration by step 2 and the right arrow is a fibration by the assumed Reedy fibrancy of $B'$. The weak factorization system $(C\cap W,F)$ of this model category therefore gives a diagonal $b:TB\to B'$ with $b\circ T(i)=i'\circ\operatorname{const}(r)$. This is a morphism in the functor category, hence is natural in every simplex map.

source.place: Hovey Theorem 5.2.5, printed pp.125-126, Reedy lifting axiom; compare the dual lifting construction of Lemma 5.5.1, printed p.133.

proof.text: In degree zero the lift equation reads $b_0\circ T(i_0)=i'_0\circ r$. Both $i_0$ and $i'_0$ are identities by assumption, and $T$ preserves identities, so $b_0=r$. For every $n\geq0$ the same equation is $b_n\circ T(i_n)=i'_n\circ r$. Here $T(i_n)$ is a weak equivalence by step 2, $i'_n$ is one by the assumed objectwise weak-equivalence coaugmentation, and $r$ is one since it is a trivial cofibration. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] first makes $i'_n\circ r$ a weak equivalence, then makes $b_n$ a weak equivalence. This proves every asserted clause with the prescribed degree-zero component.

source.place: Hovey model-category two-out-of-three axiom (Definition 1.1.3), and Lemma 5.5.1, printed p.133, degree-zero comparison.
